headline: Revolution is rapid, fundamental change—when gradual evolution isn't fast enough
universal_truth: Systems that can't adapt gradually eventually break and reform suddenly; change is inevitable, form is not
fun_facts: Most revolutions fail or produce unexpected results—the French Revolution led to Napoleon, not democracy
The Industrial Revolution changed more about daily life in 100 years than the previous 1,000
Technological revolutions are accelerating—the time between major shifts keeps shrinking
discussion_questions: What in your life has changed suddenly rather than gradually?
When is revolution necessary versus destructive?
How do you prepare for rapid change?

hook.script: For centuries, nothing much changed. Your life looked like your grandparents' lives. Then: industrial revolution, digital revolution, information revolution—each one faster than the last. Sudden, fundamental change is now the norm, not the exception.

cliff.script: We prefer gradual change—it's easier to adapt. But sometimes systems can't evolve fast enough. What makes revolution happen instead of evolution?

options.text: Revolution happens when pressure for change builds faster than systems can adapt—when gradual evolution is blocked or too slow, sudden transformation becomes inevitable
options.response: Yes. Systems that resist small changes accumulate pressure until they break. Revolution is often the cost of refusing to evolve. Flexibility prevents rupture.

options.text: Revolutions are caused by leaders who drive change
options.response: Leaders matter, but they usually ride waves of accumulated pressure rather than creating them...

fact1.title: Pressure Accumulation
fact1.script: Revolutions rarely come from nowhere. Pressure builds for years or decades—economic stress, social frustration, technological possibility. What looks sudden was actually slow accumulation reaching critical mass.

fact2.title: Unpredictable Outcomes
fact2.script: Revolutions rarely end where they intended. The French Revolution produced Napoleon. The Russian Revolution produced Stalin. Rapid change is hard to control. Be careful what you wish for when systems break.

fact3.title: Personal Revolution
fact3.script: You can experience personal revolution too—sudden life changes, career pivots, relationship shifts. Sometimes gradual change isn't possible. The skill is navigating rapid change without losing yourself.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Systems that can't adapt gradually eventually break and reform suddenly. Change is inevitable; form is not. Build flexibility to avoid rupture.

outro.script: That's Day 211. Tomorrow, we'll explore how life changes over time—evolution. Until then, consider where pressure is building in your life.

growTrack.title: Pressure Scan - Where Is Change Building?
growTrack.activity: Where in your life is pressure building—frustration, dissatisfaction, need for change that you've been delaying? Can you make gradual changes now, or is revolutionary change becoming necessary? Proactive evolution beats forced revolution.
